findings.issue: No security logging on password change success or failure. High-risk auth events must be logged with user ID and outcome for audit and incident response.

BadRequest(result.Errors) at line 43 serialises raw IdentityError objects to the client, exposing machine-readable Code values (e.g. PasswordMismatch, PasswordRequiresDigit) that reveal internal password policy and Identity error taxonomy.

Refresh tokens are not revoked after a successful password change. AccountController does not inject DbContext and makes no attempt to delete RefreshToken rows. An attacker with a stolen refresh token can continue acquiring access tokens after the victim changes their password.
findings.reference: Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.md § Change Password Feature — Reauthentication After Risk Events

findings.issue: ChangePasswordDTO (Models/AuthDTO.cs:23) has no [Required] or [StringLength] validation attributes. Model validation passes with empty/missing fields, delegating all enforcement to Identity internals rather than failing fast at the controller boundary.
findings.reference: Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.md § Implement Proper Password Strength Controls
